- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or is weak (negative sentiment → model fails to adjust downward).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then drifts back too slowly or too far.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–2 days after true price bottoms or tops.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits recent noise, ignoring longer-term trend.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast slope; if consistently positive, slightly increase but cap at 10% above recent high.
- Avoid sharp upward revisions after recent lows — model tends to “rebound” too aggressively, missing correction zones.
- If true price drops >5% from recent high, model often fails to recognize it as a structural shift, leading to delayed correction.
